title: Level on points. Who goes through?
idea: pure utility clip — works even for people who never buy anything
hook: Two teams finish level on points. Who goes through?

shots.title: LEVEL ON POINTS
shots.voice: Two teams finish the group level on points. Who goes through? Here is the order that settles it.

shots.title: 01 — GOAL DIFFERENCE
shots.voice: First, goal difference. Scored minus conceded across every group match. Not head to head — all of them.

shots.title: 02 — GOALS SCORED
shots.voice: Second, if the difference is level too, the team that scored more goes through. Attacking sides get the benefit.

shots.title: 03 — HEAD TO HEAD
shots.voice: Third, head to head. A lot of people put this first, and that is a mistake. With three teams level it forms a loop and stops working.

shots.title: WRITE IT BEFORE KICKOFF
shots.voice: And the part that matters most: this order goes in writing before the first match. Decided afterwards, it always looks like it favours someone.

shots.title: LINK IN BIO
shots.voice: One page of rules in the group chat removes almost every argument. Tell me in the comments what comes first in yours.

caption:
Level on points — who goes through?

The tiebreaker order that settles the most common argument in amateur sport, and why head-to-head should not be first.

What comes first in your rules?
